text: Hello, dear students, nice to meet you again.Today, we are going to move on to the fourth period of this unit, that is, grammar activity.By the end of this period, you are expected to consolidate the passive voices you have learned before, recognize and understand the passive in the past continuous and the past perfect in the passage, and use the passive correctly in the context.These are the pages you need for today's period.Please make sure you get the textbook and the worksheet ready.Now, let's get started.First, let's compare the two sentences here.What's the difference between the meaning and the function?You have 30 seconds.The function of was repaired is to indicate a result by stating the fact that the repairs to the car were completed and the car is now probably ready to use.While the function of was being repaired is to indicate a process and action.It is stating that the action was happening at that time, and it is not clear whether the repair work is finished or not.And with being here, I guess you might have already come up with the name of that.It's past continuous passive.As you can infer from the second sentence, this is the structure.The subject plus was or were plus being and past participle.Just like the example.The windows were being cleaned when I was there.Then, let's analyze another group of sentences.Focus on their predicates.Which action happened first?You have 10 seconds for that, please.In 1960, the cottage was turned into a school.Before that, it was used as a storehouse.The action was completed before another past time or action.That's why we have the past perfect passive.And the structure is the subject plus had been and past participle.From the two structures presented here, it may be easier for you to reach the conclusion that the difference between the passives in different tenses lies in the tenses of 必.After learning these two structures, your knowledge of the passive may have been refreshed.Then, let's read today's story.Fair trade.To check your command of the voice.What is fair trade?Fair trade refers to the practice of buying goods directly from producers in developing countries at a fair price.The movement is meant to improve the working and living conditions for the communities in developing countries by ensuring fair payment for farmers and producers.The story shows us its development.While reading, would you please take a closer look at the number of sentences?Match them to the grammar items A to G.And write down the passive form of the verb in the third column of the table on page 48.And you will have three minutes to finish the task.Let's go.The movement is meant to improve the working and living conditions for the communities in developing
